A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ODI-Bench and Omni-CoT. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite added experiments, reflow, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 20 MLLMs, Omni-CoT experiments, component ablations, and additional quantitative and qualitative results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds input-format comparisons, sensitivity analyses, repeated-run results, and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains six-view captioning, viewpoint-guided answering, crop grounding and relevance filtering, and response refinement. Its equations and prompts are unchanged. The additional component and FoV experiments test the existing framework rather than introduce a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2,000 indoor/outdoor ODIs and 4,254 QA pairs across ten tasks. The added multi-view, synthetic-video, resizing, and prompt experiments reuse these scenes and questions through different evaluation procedures. No additional dataset, population, or underlying task is evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds multi-view input comparisons for GPT-4o, Gemini-2.0-flash, and InternVL2.5-8B, plus video-input comparisons for the latter two models in Table 7. Table 14 also extends Zero-shot CoT comparisons to InternVL2.5-8B and o3. These substantially broaden the inference alternatives evaluated against Omni-CoT; the original 20-model benchmark remains intact.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 12 oriented perspective views, 12-second videos at 60 FPS, 80/90/100-degree FoV comparisons, 512×1024 downsampling, alternative GPT-4o prompt prefixes, and latency evaluation. These substantially extend the experimental controls. The original benchmark metrics and primary evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table 5 expands the sequential crop-refinement ablation with additional component combinations. New analyses test FoV selection, crop-filtering rates, resolution sensitivity, prompt sensitivity, and accuracy versus inference time (Tables 6 and 10–14). Existing error cases, qualitative comparisons, and open-ended Omni-CoT evaluation are retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run uncertainty analysis. v2 adds three-run results, means, and standard deviations for GPT-4o and InternVL2.5-8B in Table 12, a limited addition without uncertainty estimates for Omni-CoT gains. Some summaries are inconsistent: InternVL's reported human-attribute mean/SD of 70.28/0.18 do not match its displayed runs.

E6.justification: Primary scores in Tables 2–4 and the former appendix Tables 6–7, now Tables 8–9, are retained. Numerous new results cover component variants, input formats, sensitivity, filtering, repetitions, and latency. For example, Table 11 reports downsampled overall scores of 54.08 for GPT-4o and 55.52 for InternVL3-78B; Table 14 reports InternVL2.5-8B latency of 3.44 seconds for direct answering versus 13.81 seconds for full Omni-CoT. These are additional results under specified conditions, not improved headline scores between versions.

T1.justification: The spherical-coordinate and crop-FoV equations (1)–(3) are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the ten-task ODI benchmark, evaluation of 20 MLLMs revealing immersive-understanding weaknesses, and a training-free Omni-CoT framework that improves performance. Additional validation does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation: Appendix D.5 explains resolution sensitivity through fine-detail loss versus global spatial layout; D.6–D.7 discuss benchmark stability and the insufficiency of more explicit prompts; D.8 assesses the accuracy–latency tradeoff. Section 5.2.3 interprets limitations of alternative input pipelines. Appendix F also newly asserts pre-training and post-training utility, without corresponding training experiments.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a specific repository address for the planned code/data release and adds CC BY 4.0 release terms in Appendix G. It also documents the new view/video construction settings and reports inference times. Core annotation procedures and prompts are retained. The release statements remain prospective rather than establishing resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liao et al.'s visual-token-compression evaluation work and Yang et al.'s VisionThink, using them to motivate the resizing experiment in Appendix D.5. The main related-work discussion and positioning against existing ODI benchmarks remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the overall section order are retained. v2 subdivides Section 5.2, extends Appendix D, adds acknowledgements and a licensing appendix, and updates affiliations and conference headers. Local edits clarify terminology and correct the Table 1 name from 360Bench to ODI-Bench; there is no pervasive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven tables (6, 7, and 10–14) and transforms Table 5 from a compact sequential ablation into a larger component-checkmark matrix. Figure 1 gains explicit panel labels and a revised caption. Existing appendix tables and figures are largely retained, with renumbering and reflow around the substantial new tabular material.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked multi-view/video comparators and direct tests of resolution and prompt sensitivity. v2 adds these controls, expands component ablations, and exposes inference costs, substantially strengthening the evidence for both Omni-CoT and the benchmark's design. Table 12's inconsistent summary statistics and limited uncertainty coverage weaken the new stability evidence, but do not outweigh the broader gains in experimental validation.
